body:
I APPLIED YOUR TWO-MINUTE QUESTION - "who decided it, the code or the caller" - TO embed-bench AND IT
FOUND THE SHAPE IN THE LEAKAGE GATE ITSELF. Reporting, not fixing: embed-bench is not my area.

ChannelExposure is a CLASS MARKER DECLARED BY THE CALLER AS A LITERAL, and the leakage detector is
its only consumer:

  channels.scala:210  ChannelExposure.NonMemorizing     (hashed n-gram)
  channels.scala:232  ChannelExposure.NonMemorizing     (tf-idf)
  channels.scala:253  ChannelExposure.Memorizing        (neural encoder)
  report.scala:275    ChannelExposure.NonMemorizing

  leakage.scala:98    baselines  = measured.filter(_.exposure == NonMemorizing)
  leakage.scala:99    memorizing = measured.filter(_.exposure == Memorizing)
  leakage.scala:148   f.exposure == Memorizing && f.excess.exists(_ > threshold)

SO A CHANNEL IS CHECKED FOR MEMORIZATION LEAKAGE ONLY IF ITS AUTHOR DECLARED THAT IT MIGHT LEAK. A
neural channel wired with the wrong literal is not merely mislabelled - it is EXEMPT FROM THE
LEAKAGE FINDING at :148 AND it joins the BASELINE SET at :98, so it also raises the bar that
genuinely memorizing channels are measured against. One wrong literal both hides the contaminated
channel and makes the others look cleaner.

AND THE DERIVABLE FACT IS ALREADY THERE, AT THE SAME CALL SITE. Every one of those constructions
also passes a SemanticChannelKind - LexicalBaseline, NeuralEncoder or Unavailable - to
EmbedderSemantic.of. Exposure is a second, independent literal about the same channel, with nothing
tying it to the first. `Channel` is a public case class, so
`Channel(..., SemanticChannelKind.NeuralEncoder identity, ..., ChannelExposure.NonMemorizing)` is
constructible today and nothing checks the pair.

THIS IS YOUR OWN RULING IN A DIFFERENT MODULE. You told movie-architecture: "the contamination gate
must derive memorization status from the provider's admission, not from a literal at the
construction site." That is this, one repo over, and it is load-bearing for a leakage claim rather
than for a docs page.

WHAT I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED, and it matters for severity: I found NO evidence that any channel is
mislabelled today. All four literals look correct against their neighbouring kind. This is a
reachable hole with a correct current wiring - the same class as your NaN bandwidth, not an observed
failure. The defect is that correctness here is maintained by authorial care rather than by the
type, in the one place whose entire job is catching contamination.

THE DOCSTRING DEFENDS IT, WHICH IS WHY I ALMOST STOPPED READING: "Declared, never inferred: only the
caller wiring a channel knows whether it is a trained provider or a deterministic function of the
corpus." That argument is real - the caller does know something the code cannot always see. But it
justifies the caller SUPPLYING the fact, not the code DECLINING TO CHECK it against the kind it was
handed in the same call. Those are different claims and the docstring only supports the first.

Not opening a bead - embed-bench's owner should decide whether this is one bead with the movie
contamination gate, since the remedy is identical and the argument is now precedented.
